pages.title: Grim Storage Industries
text: Simple storage that grows all the way to the end game. Everything you store lives in one network, and the network can craft for you.
There are **no channels, no byte limits and no cable rules**. Any network block that touches another network block joins it.
Use the **arrows** at the bottom, the arrow keys, or your mouse wheel to turn pages. Pick a chapter on the left to jump around.

pages.title: Your first hour
text: - Find **Soulite Ore** underground and smelt it into ingots.
- Craft a **Network Controller**, a **Soul Drive**, a **Copper Storage Cell** and a **Soul Terminal**.
- Put the cell in the drive, place everything touching, and open the terminal.
That is a working storage system. The rest of this book shows how to grow it.

pages.title: Lost this book?
pages.text: Craft a new one from any book and a Soulite Ingot.

pages.title: Finding Soulite
text: Soulite is a pale blue ore that glows faintly and chimes when broken. Mine it with an **iron pickaxe** or better.
- **Overworld:** Y -48 to 16, most common around Y -16. Stone and deepslate versions.
- **Nether:** inside the soul sand and soul soil of **Soul Sand Valleys**. These drop 2 to 3 Raw Soulite.
- **Deep Dark:** rare **Echo Soulite Ore** near the sculk. Needs a diamond pickaxe. You will need it for late tiers.
Fortune works on all of them.

pages.title: Smelting
pages.text: Smelt or blast Raw Soulite into ingots. Nine ingots make a Block of Soulite, and nine nuggets make an ingot.

pages.title: The Soul Infuser
text: Your first machine. Put in a **Soulite Ingot**, **Soul Sand** (or soul soil) and **Nether Quartz**, in any slots, to make **Infused Soulite**. No fuel needed.
Pipes and hoppers can feed it from any side and pull the result out.

pages.title: Infused Soulite
text: Made in the Soul Infuser. It unlocks the third tier: Diamond cells, Speed Upgrades, the Stock Keeper and wireless terminals.
With **JEI** installed, look up Infused Soulite (or click the arrow in the Soul Infuser) to see every infusing recipe.

pages.title: Echo Soulite Alloy
pages.text: One Infused Soulite, two Echo Soulite Shards from the Deep Dark, and a Netherite Scrap. This is the fourth tier.

pages.title: Singularity Core
pages.text: Eight Echo Soulite Alloys around a Nether Star. The end-game trophy, used for Singularity Cells and the Singularity Terminal.

pages.title: Network Controller
text: The heart of a network. Every network needs **exactly one**. With two connected, the network stops and the controller tells you why.
Open it to see how full your storage is, how many cells and drives you have, and every crafting job (with a button to cancel each).

pages.title: Soul Drive
pages.text: Holds 8 storage cells of any kind. Cells keep everything inside them, even when you take them out or move them to another drive.

pages.title: Soul Terminal
pages.text: Where you see, take and store everything. The next chapter explains it in full.

pages.title: Connecting things
text: Network blocks join just by touching. To reach further, use **Soul Cable**, or **Soulite Glass** if you want it to look nice.
One cable carries **everything**: items, fluids, energy, XP, chemicals and Source all travel down the same line to every bus, interface and machine on the network.
There is no limit on how many blocks a network can have.

pages.title: Soul Wrench
text: A handy tool for tidying up your network.
- **Click a cable connection** to cut it, so two cables (or a cable and a block) stop joining. Click the same side again to join it back.
- **Click a bus on a cable** to take the bus off.
- **Click a machine** to turn it to face the side you clicked. Works on most machines from other mods too.
- **Sneak-click** any Grim Storage block to pick it up.

pages.title: Who can use it
text: The player who places a **Network Controller** owns the network. Nobody else can open its blocks, use a wireless terminal on it, or break or add its blocks.
Open the controller and click the **key** to trust other players by name, or to open the network to everyone.
A network nobody owns (built before this, or placed by a machine) is open, and anyone can **claim** it there. Server operators can always get in.

pages.title: Taking and storing
text: - **Click** an item to take a stack.
- **Right-click** to take half a stack.
- **Shift-click** to send a stack straight to your inventory.
- **Click with an item held** to store it (right-click stores one).
- **Shift-click** anything in your own inventory to store it.

pages.title: Shift keeps things still
text: While you **hold Shift**, nothing in the terminal moves. Shift-click the same spot again and again to keep taking the same item.
An item that runs out stays in its spot, faded, until you let go. Let go of Shift and the list sorts itself again.

pages.title: Finding things
text: Type in the search box to filter. Start with `@` to search by mod, for example `@mekanism`. Right-click the box to clear it.
The button next to it changes the sort: by amount, by name, by mod or **recently added**. **Alt-click** an item to **pin** it to the top.

The **tabs on the left** filter by type: ores, ingots, weapons and tools, armor, food, mob drops, farming, building blocks and misc. The last one, **Craftable**, shows only what your network can craft.

pages.title: Crafting grid
text: The terminal has its own 3x3 crafting grid on the right. Put ingredients in and take the result.
When a slot runs out, it **refills itself from storage**, so you can keep crafting. **Shift-click** the result to craft a full stack at once.
The small **x** puts everything in the grid back into storage. Closing the terminal does the same.
With JEI, press **+** on a crafting recipe to fill the grid from storage. Missing ingredients show red. The **pencil** writes the grid's recipe on a Recipe Card you carry; the items stay put.

pages.title: Crafting jobs
text: The **last tab along the top** shows everything the network is crafting right now.
Each job shows how far along it is and what it is waiting for. Under it, every step: which machine makes it, how many are done and how many are **in machines** right now.
The buttons on a job **move it up or down**, **pause** it, or **cancel** it (the **x**). Anything already made stays in storage.

pages.title: The queue
text: Jobs at the **top** get the Soul Assemblers and machines first. **Shift-click** the up arrow to send a job straight to the top.
A **paused** job (yellow edge) waits and takes nothing until you press play.
On shared networks each player can run **16 jobs** at once, so one big order can't block everyone (pack makers can change it in the config).

pages.title: Terminal settings
text: Click the **gear** at the top of the terminal:
- **Sync search with JEI:** the terminal and JEI share one search.
- **Type to search on open:** start typing as soon as it opens.
- **Keep search when closed:** your search is still there next time.
- **Size:** Auto fits your screen. Normal, Tall and Taller show 6, 9 or 12 rows.

pages.title: Resource tabs
text: The tabs **along the top** switch what the terminal shows.
- **Everything** (the drive icon, first tab): items, fluids, chemicals, energy, Source and XP all in one list. Click them just like in their own tabs.
- **Items**, then one tab each for **Fluids, Chemicals, Energy, Source and Experience**.
See the chapter on fluids, energy and more for how to fill and empty buckets and tanks.

pages.title: Dark or light
text: Every screen in this mod has a small **moon or sun** in its top-right corner. Click it to switch between dark and light. It remembers your choice.
You can also change how see-through the screens are from the mod's **Config** button in the mod list.

pages.title: Item cells
text: Cells count items, not types. Any mix of items is fine.
- **Copper:** 4,096 items
- **Gold:** 65,536 items
- **Diamond:** about 1 million items
- **Netherite:** about 67 million items
Hover over a cell to see how full it is.

pages.title: Bigger cells
pages.text: Gold cells use Gold and a Block of Soulite. Diamond cells need Infused Soulite, and Netherite cells need Echo Soulite Alloy.

pages.title: Telling tiers apart
text: Every tier has its own **cap color** and **1 to 4 lights** down the right side: Copper, Gold, Diamond, Netherite.
- **Diamond** cells catch the light with a moving shine.
- **Netherite** cells glow with ember seams and shimmer like enchanted gear.
Names and tooltips get brighter colors at each tier, so you can spot your best cells at a glance.

pages.title: Singularity Cell
text: Holds **one item type with no limit**. Great for cobblestone, dirt or anything you farm in huge amounts.
To choose its item, hold that item in your **off hand** and use the cell. Sneak and use an empty cell to unlock it.
Items always go to a matching Singularity Cell first.

pages.title: More than items
text: The network can also store **fluids**, **energy (FE)**, **experience (XP)**, Mekanism **chemicals** and Ars Nouveau **Source**. Each has its own cells, and they all go in the same Soul Drive.
Chemical cells need Mekanism and Source cells need Ars Nouveau. Without those mods, those cells simply do not appear.

pages.title: Sizes
text: - **Fluid and chemical cells:** 256, 4,096, 65,536 and about a million buckets.
- **Energy cells:** 16M, 256M, 4B and 64B FE.
- **Source cells:** 10k, 100k, 1M and 10M Source.
- **Experience cells:** 100k, 2M, 50M and 2B XP.
They use the same Copper, Gold, Diamond and Netherite tiers as item cells.

pages.title: In the terminal
text: Use the tabs along the top of the terminal.
- **Fill a bucket or tank:** hold it empty and click a fluid.
- **Store a fluid:** hold a full bucket or tank and click anywhere in the list.
Chemicals work the same way with Mekanism tanks. Energy and Source show as one big gauge.

pages.title: Experience
text: XP is stored in points. In the **Experience** tab: **click** to take a level, **shift-click** for 10 levels, and **right-click** to store all of your XP.
Liquid XP from other mods is turned into points automatically (20 mB per point), and an **Import Bus** under a mob farm soaks up XP orbs.

pages.title: Pipes and machines
text: The easy way: stick an **Import Bus** on a machine, tank or generator and everything in it flows into the network. An **Export Bus** sends things back out. Pipes from any mod can plug into either bus too. See the Buses chapter.
Pipes can also push anything into a **Network Interface**. To let pipes **pull** from it, open it and turn on that resource's **Pull** switch.

pages.title: How it works
text: Teach the network a recipe with a **Recipe Card**, then put the card in a **Soul Assembler** on the network.

Now that item shows in the terminal with a **Craft** label. Click it, type how many, and the network does the rest. It uses what it has, crafts any ingredients it can, and tells you exactly what is missing if it cannot.

pages.title: Recipe Cards
text: Use a blank card to open its grid. **Click items into the grid** to set the recipe. They are only pictures; nothing is used up. The result appears on the right.
Sneak and use a card to wipe it. Hold just one card at a time to edit it.

pages.title: Any planks will do
text: A Recipe Card uses **any variant** the recipe takes. A chest card made with oak planks also crafts from birch, spruce or any other planks you have.
The **Any / Exact** button at the top of the card switches this off, for when it must be exactly the items on the card.

pages.title: Cards from JEI or EMI
text: You don't need the items to write a card.
- Open the card, then find the recipe in **JEI, EMI or REI** and press its **+** button. The card is written.
- Or **drag** items from JEI's list onto the card's slots. This works on every filter slot too.
- **Processing Cards** take the + button on a recipe of **any mod**: what goes in and what comes out are both filled in.
- In the terminal, the **pencil** next to the crafting grid writes the grid's recipe on a Recipe Card you carry.

pages.title: Soul Assembler
text: Holds 9 Recipe Cards. Add more assemblers for more recipes.
Each **Speed Upgrade** doubles its speed, up to 4 for 16x.

pages.title: Speed Upgrade
pages.text: Made with Infused Soulite, glowstone and redstone. Speeds up a Soul Assembler (doubling each time, up to 4) and Import and Export Buses (up to 8).

pages.title: Ordering crafts
text: - Items with **0 stored** show **Craft**. Just click them.
- To craft more of something you already have, **ctrl-click** or **middle-click** it.
- Watch or cancel jobs in the **Network Controller**.
If storage is full, the job pauses and says so.
Before it starts, the order window shows the **whole plan**: every step and what makes it, what it takes from storage, anything **missing** in red, and about how long it will take.
When a craft you ordered finishes (or has been stuck for a minute), a **pop-up** in the corner tells you, wherever you are.

pages.title: Using any machine
text: Autocrafting can also use **furnaces and machines from any mod**.
Write the machine's recipe on a **Processing Card**: what goes in on the left, what comes back on the right. Click with a stack to set an amount; right-click adds one.

pages.title: Processing Interface
text: Place it against the machine. Its front faces whatever block you clicked when placing it.
Put Processing Cards in it. The network sends the inputs into the machine and pulls the results back out by itself.

pages.title: Machine Bus
text: The **Machine Bus** clips onto a machine, like an Import Bus. The network then uses that machine for autocrafting.
It needs no cards on **furnaces, smokers and blast furnaces** or on **machines from big mods**: it learns every recipe the machine can make. They show up in the **Craftable** tab.

pages.title: Machine Bus tricks
text: - **Keeps machines going:** furnaces get fuel and powered machines get energy from your network.
- Takes back everything a machine makes, extras like **sawdust** too, so it never clogs.
- **Several buses on several furnaces share big jobs**: 64 ore on 4 furnaces cooks 4 times as fast.
- Holds 9 Processing Cards for **any other machine**.
- Buttons in its screen turn learning and fuelling off.

pages.title: Modded machines
text: The Machine Bus learns recipes from **Mekanism** (all its item machines and factories, the Purification Chamber and Osmium Compressor too), **Create** (Millstone), **Ender IO** (SAG Mill, Alloy Smelter), **Ars Nouveau** (Imbuement Chamber), **Immersive Engineering**, **Powah**, **Modern Industrialization**, **Oritech** and **Actually Additions**.
Other mods' machines often work too when the machine's name matches its recipes (a crusher crushes).
On Mekanism machines it opens the side it touches by itself. No Configurator needed.

pages.title: Good to know
text: - Recipes that need a **fluid or a chemical** work too: the bus fills the machine's tanks from your network. Mekanism chemicals that come from items (**redstone dust** for infusing) are sent as those items.
- Machines that need a part to run (an Ender IO capacitor, a Create motor) still need it.
- **Pack makers:** add any machine in a datapack: `data/<pack>/grimstorage_machines/<name>.json` with `"machines"` and `"recipe_types"` lists.
- Need something special? A **Processing Card** in the bus still works for any machine.

pages.title: Chemical chains
text: Machines that make **fluids or chemicals** work too: the bus pulls them back into your fluid and chemical cells.
So whole lines plan in one go. Order **Iron Crystals** and the network runs the **Chemical Washer**, then the **Crystallizer**, each with its own bus.
Works with Mekanism's Dissolution Chamber, Washer, Crystallizer, Oxidizer, Infuser, Separator, Centrifuge, Reaction Chamber and more.

pages.title: Source machines
text: Put a **Source cell** in a drive and a Machine Bus on an Ars Nouveau **Imbuement Chamber**: the bus gives it exactly the Source each recipe costs, no jars needed.
Recipes that need items on **pedestals** around the chamber are left out: the network can't place those for you.

pages.title: Example
text: To autocraft Infused Soulite:
- Place a Processing Interface touching a **Soul Infuser**.
- Make a card with Soulite Ingot, Soul Sand and Quartz in, and Infused Soulite out.
- Put the card in the interface.
Infused Soulite now shows as craftable in the terminal.

pages.title: Stock Keeper
text: Keeps an amount of something crafted, for example **always 500 iron gears**.
Click an item into one of its 9 slots, click the number under it, type how many to keep and press **Set**. When stock drops below that, it crafts more.
The dot over each item is green when stocked, blue while crafting, and red when something is missing.

pages.title: Void Filter
text: Pick up to 9 items. When storage is **full**, those items are destroyed instead of backing up your farms.
Only the extra is destroyed. Nothing is deleted while there is still room.

pages.title: Network Interface
text: Lets pipes, hoppers and other mods use the network. Anything pushed in is stored.
Things can only be pulled **out** if you allow it: put items in its 9 slots, or turn on the **Pull** switches for fluids, energy, chemicals, Source and XP.
Works with Grim Pipe Industries and other pipe mods. For no pipes at all, use an Import or Export Bus.

pages.title: Chest Link
text: The **Chest Link** clips onto a chest, barrel, drawer or any inventory and makes it part of your storage. Its items show in the terminal, crafts use them, and new items can go in.
In its screen: **in and out**, **only put in** or **only take out**, and whether it fills up **before your cells**.

pages.title: Redstone Emitter
text: Pick an item and an amount. The **Redstone Emitter** gives a redstone signal when the network has **at least** that many, or **fewer** (switch a mob farm off at 10,000 bones).
Set to **Craft while powered**, it does the opposite: while it gets a redstone signal, it crafts the item up to that amount.

pages.title: Buses
text: - **Import Bus** (cyan): takes things **out of the block, into your network**. Use it to empty a chest.
- **Export Bus** (orange): sends things **from your network into the block**, only what you pick.
Put one on the end of a Soul Cable (next page), or on any block by itself with cable to its back.
Wrong one? Right-click it and click the direction button to switch.

pages.title: Buses on cable
text: Run **Soul Cable** from your drive, terminal, interface or any network block up to a chest or machine.
Then **use the bus on that chest** (or on the end of the cable). It goes onto the cable, facing the chest, and everything flows straight into the network.
- **Right-click** the bus to open its filter screen.
- **Break** the bus to take just the bus off. The cable stays.
Each side of a cable can hold one bus. The network never passes through a side with a bus on it.

pages.title: Import Bus
text: Pulls **everything** by default: items, fluids, energy, XP, chemicals and Source, all from one bus.
Put one on a generator to store its power, on a tank to empty it, or on a furnace to collect what it smelts.
Facing **open air**, it picks up dropped items and **XP orbs** in that block. Put it under a mob farm.

pages.title: Export Bus
text: Sends out **only the items you pick** in its filter by default, so it never empties your storage by accident.
Switch on fluids, energy, XP, chemicals or Source to send those too. Energy, Source and XP do not need a filter.
Example: an Export Bus on a furnace with coal in its filter keeps it fuelled.

pages.title: Pipes from any mod
text: Pipes from any mod connect straight to a bus, on **any side**.
- Pipes **push into an Import Bus** and it all goes into the network.
- Pipes **pull out of an Export Bus**, but only what its filter and switches allow.
Works for items, fluids, energy, chemicals, Source and liquid XP. Run Soul Cable to the back of the bus and one line carries it all.
If a bus faces straight into a pipe, set that pipe end to **pull** (in your pipe mod) to take from an Export Bus. Pipes push into an Import Bus as normal.

pages.title: Filters
text: Open a bus to set it up. Click items into the **9 filter slots**. A bucket or tank filters the fluid or chemical inside it.
- **Only these:** just what is in the filter moves.
- **All but these:** everything moves except what is in the filter.
- **Exact match / Ignore NBT:** whether enchantments and other item data must match.

pages.title: Resource switches
text: The icons in the middle turn each resource **on or off** for that bus: Items, Fluids, Chemicals, Energy, Source and XP. A green line means it is on.
The top right shows what the bus is doing: **Working**, **Idle**, **Storage full**, **No network** or **Nothing attached**.

pages.title: Speed Upgrades
text: Put **Speed Upgrades** in the slots on the right of a bus's screen, up to **8**.
Each one adds the bus's base speed again: **1 upgrade = 2x**, **8 upgrades = 9x**. A fully upgraded bus moves over **1,000 items** or **288 buckets** every tick.
Upgrades stay with the bus, and drop when you take it off.

pages.title: Fast and light
text: A busy bus moves up to **128 items** or **32 buckets** every tick, and as much energy as the machine allows.
When there is nothing to move it slows down to check about once a second, and wakes up right away when something next to it changes. Hundreds of buses are fine.

pages.title: Wireless Terminal
text: A terminal in your pocket. **Sneak and use it on a Network Controller** to link it, then use it anywhere within 128 blocks in the same dimension.
It has the same tabs and crafting grid as the block.

pages.title: Singularity Terminal
pages.text: Works at any distance, in any dimension.

pages.title: Quick dump
text: Carrying a linked wireless terminal? Press **G** to send your whole main inventory into storage. Your hotbar and armor stay put.
Change the key in Controls, under Grim Storage Industries.

pages.title: Quantum Link
text: Joins two places into one network, at any distance or across dimensions. Crafting makes a pair.
Use a **Soul Tether** on the first link, then on the second. Sneak and use the tether on a link to unpair it.
Both ends must be loaded to connect, so use a chunk loader for far-away bases.

pages.title: The five tiers
text: - **1. Soulite Ingot:** controller, drive, terminal, cable, glass, interface, Import and Export Bus, Copper cells, Soul Infuser.
- **2. Soulite and Gold:** Gold cells, Recipe Cards, Soul Assembler, Void Filter.
- **3. Infused Soulite:** Diamond cells, Speed Upgrade, Stock Keeper, Wireless Terminal, Processing Card.
- **4. Echo Soulite Alloy:** Netherite cells, Processing Interface, Quantum Link.
- **5. Singularity Core:** Singularity Cell, Singularity Terminal.

pages.title: Something is wrong
text: - **Terminal says no working network:** check the controller is connected and there is only one.
- **Items will not go in:** storage is full. Add cells, or a Void Filter for junk.
- **A craft never finishes:** open the controller to see what it is waiting for, and cancel it if needed.
- **A bus says Nothing attached or Idle:** check it is on the right face, its resource switches are on, and (Export Bus) its filter has something in it.
- **Wireless terminal will not open:** link it again, and stay in range.

pages.title: Good to know
text: - Crafting jobs in progress stop if the world closes. Stored items are always saved.
- Quantum Links need both ends loaded.
- Autocrafting works with items. Fluids, energy, XP, chemicals and Source are stored and moved, not crafted.
- New Mekanism tanks and machines start with their sides closed. Open the side the bus touches with a **Configurator**.
Made by xTri6 for Nine Craft.
